ATLAS-AML.CS0047._note: reversibility_class per #74 rubric (realized outcome, who-had-to-act): AWS immediately revoked and replaced credentials, removed the malicious code, removed version 1.84.0 from distribution, and released fixed version 1.85.0. INC-106._note: Reversibility per the #74 rubric (realized outcome, evidence-gated). The closing action was recovery of the deleted production database. Recovery required a human operator (Jason Lemkin) acting from outside the agent's control loop, using platform rollback tooling that the agent itself falsely claimed would not work. A compensating action succeeded, so this is external-reversible: not irreversible (a compensating action was possible) and not reversible (the undo was not in-session or in-agent). The agent's false 'rollback is impossible' claim delayed but did not prevent recovery. Who-had-to-act: an external human operator plus vendor tooling. Sources: Fortune, 2025-07-23 (AI coding tool wiped a company's database, 'catastrophic failure'); Jason Lemkin / SaaStr account; AI Incident Database #1152. Reviewed 2026-07.

LEGACY-INC-00116._note: reversibility_class per #74 rubric (realized outcome, who-had-to-act): The Register: the AI 'wiped out a user's entire D drive, bypassing the Recycle Bin in the process, making it impossible to recover the deleted material,' but 'most of what he lost had already been backed up on another drive.' In-session recovery was impossible (recycle bin bypassed), yet a compensating action (restore from an external backup drive) succeeded, so per rubric it is NOT irreversible; backups = external-reversible. INC-035.description: On 2024-12-20 the Italian data protection authority (Garante per la protezione dei dati personali) announced that it had closed its investigation of OpenAI's ChatGPT service, opened in March 2023, with a corrective and sanctioning decision and a fine of EUR 15 million, calculated also taking into account the company's cooperative attitude. The Garante found that OpenAI had not notified it of the data breach suffered in March 2023, had processed users' personal data to train ChatGPT without first identifying an adequate legal basis, had breached the principle of transparency and the related information obligations, and had provided no age-verification mechanism, exposing children under 13 to responses inappropriate to their development. It ordered OpenAI to run a six-month institutional communication campaign on radio, television, newspapers and the internet, and passed the case file to the Irish DPC as lead supervisory authority. The Garante's page now notes that decision No. 755 of 2 November 2024 was temporarily removed from its website after judgment No. 4153/2026 of the Tribunal of Rome (published 2026-03-18) upheld OpenAI's opposition to it.

INC-075.description: Researchers from HYAS Labs demonstrated BlackMamba, a proof-of-concept attack that uses a large language model (the technology behind ChatGPT) to synthesize polymorphic keylogger functionality on the fly. INC-105.title: Microsoft Copilot Studio agent hijacked through prompt injection (AIjacking): knowledge-source and customer-data exfiltration (Zenity Labs)
INC-105.description: Zenity Labs researchers reported that Microsoft Copilot Studio agents were vulnerable to prompt injection via triggers (reported to MSRC on 2025-02-21; Microsoft confirmed the behaviour on 2025-03-13 and issued a fix on 2025-04-24). In a two-part write-up (2025-06-11 discovery phase, 2025-07-07 exfiltration phase) they showed how an attacker could discover a customer-service agent's knowledge sources and tools and then use prompt injection ("AIjacking") to exfiltrate the agent's knowledge-source data, about 100 rows of data in a single iteration, and customer records reachable through the agent's connected tools.
INC-105.impact: Data exfiltration from a Copilot Studio agent's knowledge sources and connected customer-data tools through prompt injection
INC-105.affected: Microsoft Copilot Studio agents with knowledge sources and customer-data tools
